summary: This benchmark evaluates a confidence-routed 7B-to-14B model grafting architecture on Apple Silicon using MLX, demonstrating a 1.70x paired median latency speedup over continuous blending on bracket-decoy workloads. The methodology is rigorous, featuring paired batches, cyclical repetitions, and bootstrap confidence intervals, supported by exact environment specifications and audit receipts.
strengths: Sound benchmarking methodology utilizing paired batch testing, warm-up runs, resident in-memory model weights, and measurement of full routing overhead.
Rigorous statistical reporting using medians and 5,000-iteration bootstrap confidence intervals for both speedup ratios and task accuracy.
Meticulous documentation of hardware specifications (Apple M5 Ultra Studio with 256 GiB unified memory), OS build, and library versions (MLX 0.32.4 / MLX-LM 0.32.2).
Honest discussion of trade-offs and bounds, explicitly noting that routing remains slower than standalone 7B and limiting claims to the tested single-token synthetic repair domain.
weaknesses: Narrow synthetic evaluation scope limited to short 4-token Python bracket-decoy repairs rather than open-ended multi-token generation.
Absence of parameter sensitivity analysis across varying logit margin routing thresholds or diverse batch sizes.
suggestions: Evaluate how the routing threshold impacts the Pareto frontier between latency speedup and completion accuracy across a broader sweep of margin cutoffs.
Extend the benchmark to multi-token autoregressive generation and standard coding evaluation suites (such as HumanEval or MBPP) to test generalizability.

claims.text: Running the 14B graft only on low-margin prompts gave a paired median speedup of 1.70× versus always blending on bracket-decoy batches (95% interval 1.68–1.76×).
claims.source: Internal experimental audit logs and reported paired batch latency distributions (420.11 ms vs 235.76 ms median batch timings)

claims.text: The route took 235.76 ms median per batch of 12 decoy prompts, while the standalone 7B took 134.72 ms.
claims.source: Internal experimental results table comparing standalone 7B, always blend, and confidence route execution times

claims.text: The owner’s Apple M5 Ultra Studio has 256 GiB unified memory. It ran macOS build 26B118, Python 3.12.16, MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2
